title: Skill and chance in association football
who: C. Reep & B. Benjamin
venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series A 131(4)
summary: Statistical analysis of passing-move lengths in 578 matches notated by Reep (1953-67); its few-pass findings were later used to justify long-ball football.

title: Modelling association football scores
who: M. J. Maher
summary: Fitted Poisson models of scores with team attacking and defensive strength parameters; the template for most later goal-based match models.

title: Opta Index founded
who: Opta Index Ltd
summary: Company founded to code Premier League match events; supplied Sky Sports in 1996-97, then became the league's official player-performance statistics provider.

title: World Football Elo Ratings
who: Bob Runyan (eloratings.net)
summary: Adapted Arpad Elo's chess rating system to international football, adding match importance, home advantage and goal margin; ratings published online.

title: RoboCup: The Robot World Cup Initiative
who: H. Kitano, M. Asada, Y. Kuniyoshi, I. Noda & E. Osawa
summary: Proposed robot soccer as a standard benchmark problem for AI and robotics, launching the RoboCup competitions for simulated and physical robot teams.

title: Modelling association football scores and inefficiencies in the football betting market
who: M. J. Dixon & S. G. Coles
venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series C 46(2)
summary: Poisson regression model with low-score dependence and time-varying team strength, fitted to 1992-95 English data and tested against bookmakers' odds.

title: Measuring the effectiveness of playing strategies at soccer
who: R. Pollard & C. Reep
venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series D (The Statistician) 46(4)
summary: Defined possession 'yield' (probability of scoring minus conceding) and applied logistic regression to shots at goal; an early precursor of xG and possession value.

title: Visualization of dominant region in team games and its application to teamwork analysis
who: T. Taki & J. Hasegawa
summary: Defined 'dominant regions': Voronoi-like areas each player can reach first, using arrival time instead of distance; a precursor of pitch-control models.

title: Testing mixed-strategy equilibria when players are heterogeneous: the case of penalty kicks in soccer
who: P.-A. Chiappori, S. Levitt & T. Groseclose
summary: Tested mixed-strategy equilibrium predictions on professional penalty-kick data; kickers' and goalkeepers' choices were broadly consistent with the theory.

title: Professionals play minimax
who: I. Palacios-Huerta
summary: Penalty kicks as a natural zero-sum game: success rates were equal across strategies and choices serially independent, as the minimax theorem predicts.

title: Moneyball: The Art of Winning an Unfair Game
who: Michael Lewis
summary: Baseball book on the Oakland Athletics' use of statistics to find undervalued players; context for later analytics adoption in football.

title: Applications of logistic regression to shots at goal in association football
who: J. Ensum, R. Pollard & S. Taylor
summary: Logistic regression of World Cup shots estimating goal probability from factors such as distance and angle; often cited (as 2004) as an early xG model.

title: Validation of Prozone: a new video-based performance analysis system
who: V. Di Salvo, A. Collins, B. McNeill & M. Cardinale
venue: International Journal of Performance Analysis in Sport 6(1)
summary: Validated speed measurements from Prozone, an early commercial multi-camera system that tracked every player during professional football matches.

title: Action bias among elite soccer goalkeepers: the case of penalty kicks
who: M. Bar-Eli, O. H. Azar, I. Ritov, Y. Keidar-Levin & G. Schein
summary: Argued goalkeepers dive although staying central looked optimal, attributing it to action bias; a 2026 replication in the same journal disputes this.

title: High-intensity running in English FA Premier League soccer matches
who: P. S. Bradley et al.
summary: Profiled high-intensity running by playing position for 370 player observations across 28 Premier League matches using multi-camera tracking.

title: Quantifying the performance of individual players in a team activity
who: J. Duch, J. S. Waitzman & L. A. N. Amaral
summary: Built passing 'flow networks' from Euro 2008 matches to quantify individual player contributions and overall team performance.

title: A framework for tactical analysis and individual offensive production assessment in soccer using Markov chains
who: S. Rudd
venue: New England Symposium on Statistics in Sports (NESSIS) 2011
summary: Modelled possessions as Markov chains over pitch states to value players' offensive actions; a precursor of Expected Threat.

title: IFAB approves goal-line technology
who: IFAB / FIFA
summary: On 5 July 2012 IFAB approved goal-line technology (Hawk-Eye and GoalRef), clearing FIFA to use it at the 2014 World Cup.

title: A network theory analysis of football strategies
who: J. López Peña & H. Touchette
summary: Built weighted, directed passing networks for 2010 World Cup teams and used centrality measures to identify key players and team play patterns.

title: Opta expected goals (xG) model
who: Sam Green (Opta)
summary: Opta analyst Sam Green introduced an xG model of shot-conversion probability, comparing 2011/12 Premier League players' goals with expected goals.

title: First MLSA workshop (Machine Learning and Data Mining for Sports Analytics)
who: MLSA organisers
summary: First edition of the ECML/PKDD sports analytics workshop (27 Sept 2013); it has since run almost annually and publishes many soccer papers.

title: Soccer video and player position dataset
who: S. A. Pettersen et al.
summary: Open dataset of synchronised video and 20 Hz ZXY body-sensor player positions from professional matches at Alfheim Stadium, Tromsø, Norway.

title: Searching for a unique style in soccer
who: L. Gyarmati, H. Kwak & P. Rodriguez
venue: KDD 2014 Workshop on Large-Scale Sports Analytics
summary: Introduced 'flow motifs' in passing networks to compare team styles; found FC Barcelona's tiki-taka has a distinctive, finely structured pattern.

title: Match analysis in football: a systematic review
who: H. Sarmento, R. Marcelino, M. T. Anguera et al.
summary: PRISMA systematic review, led by Portuguese researchers, of match-analysis research in adult men's football: topics, methods and trends.

title: Using network metrics in soccer: a macro-analysis
who: F. M. Clemente, M. S. Couceiro, F. M. L. Martins & R. S. Mendes
summary: Portuguese study proposing team-level network metrics such as density, applied to 577 offensive plays from five matches.

title: "Quality vs Quantity": Improved shot prediction in soccer using strategic features from spatiotemporal data
who: P. Lucey, A. Bialkowski, M. Monfort, P. Carr & I. Matthews
summary: Estimated chance quality using strategic features from a full season of player and ball tracking data, beyond shot location alone.

title: Physics-based modeling of pass probabilities in soccer
who: W. Spearman, A. Basye, G. Dick, R. Hotovy & P. Pop
summary: Time-to-intercept ball-control model fitted to 2015-16 Premier League tracking data; predicted the receiving team with 81% accuracy; basis of many pitch-control implementations.

title: Data-driven ghosting using deep imitation learning
who: H. M. Le, P. Carr, Y. Yue & P. Lucey
summary: Recurrent networks trained by imitation learning on tracking data predict where defenders would typically be, enabling counterfactual analysis of defensive positioning.

title: Not all passes are created equal: objectively measuring the risk and reward of passes in soccer from tracking data
who: P. Power, H. Ruiz, X. Wei & P. Lucey
summary: Graded passes on a continuous scale from tracking data by risk (likelihood of execution) and reward (likelihood of creating a chance).

title: An examination of expected goals and shot efficiency in soccer
who: A. Rathke
venue: Journal of Human Sport and Exercise 12(Proc2)
summary: Zone-based xG from 2012-13 Premier League and Bundesliga shots, using shot distance and angle to assess finishing efficiency.

title: Beyond crowd judgments: data-driven estimation of market value in association football
who: O. Müller, A. Simons & M. Weinmann
summary: Estimated players' transfer market values from performance and popularity data, as an alternative to crowdsourced (Transfermarkt-style) valuations.

title: 2017 Soccer Prediction Challenge and Open International Soccer Database
who: W. Dubitzky, P. Lopes, J. Davis & D. Berrar
summary: Open (CC0) results of 216,743 matches from 52 leagues; challenge entrants predicted 206 upcoming matches from March 2017.

title: Beyond Expected Goals
who: W. Spearman
summary: Off-ball scoring opportunity (OBSO) model combining pitch control with scoring probability to value positions of players without the ball.

title: Wide open spaces: a statistical technique for measuring space creation in professional soccer
who: J. Fernández & L. Bornn
summary: Pitch-control and pitch-value surfaces from tracking data to measure how players occupy and create valuable space, illustrated with FC Barcelona.

title: StatsBomb open data
who: StatsBomb (now Hudl StatsBomb)
summary: Free event data on GitHub, starting with 2018 women's leagues and the 2018 men's World Cup; later extended with 360 freeze-frame data.

title: FIFA adopts Elo-based SUM world ranking
who: FIFA
summary: FIFA Council approved an Elo-based 'SUM' men's ranking in June 2018, effective August 2018, replacing the averaging formula.

title: VAR approved for the 2018 FIFA World Cup
who: IFAB / FIFA
summary: IFAB added video assistant referees to the Laws on 3 March 2018; the FIFA Council then approved VAR for all 2018 World Cup matches.

title: Effective injury forecasting in soccer with GPS training data and machine learning
who: A. Rossi, L. Pappalardo, P. Cintia et al.
summary: Forecast injuries from GPS-derived training-workload features of a professional club's players over one season using machine learning.

title: SoccerNet: a scalable dataset for action spotting in soccer videos
who: S. Giancola, M. Amine, T. Dghaily & B. Ghanem
summary: Benchmark of 500 broadcast matches annotated with goals, cards and substitutions for temporal action spotting.

title: Actions speak louder than goals: valuing player actions in soccer (VAEP)
who: T. Decroos, L. Bransen, J. Van Haaren & J. Davis
summary: Introduced the SPADL action format and VAEP, valuing each on-ball action by its change in short-term scoring and conceding probabilities.

title: socceraction
who: KU Leuven DTAI (T. Decroos, P. Robberechts et al.)
summary: Python library converting provider event data to SPADL and computing VAEP and xT action values.

title: Introducing Expected Threat (xT)
who: Karun Singh
summary: Grid-based Markov model giving each pitch zone a probability of leading to a goal; passes and carries valued by the change in threat.

title: Decomposing the immeasurable sport: a deep learning expected possession value framework for soccer
who: J. Fernández, L. Bornn & D. Cervone
venue: MIT Sloan Sports Analytics Conference 2019; extended in Machine Learning 110 (2021)
summary: Expected possession value (EPV) from full tracking data, combining deep-learning components for passes, ball drives and shots in a stochastic model.

title: PlayeRank: data-driven performance evaluation and player ranking in soccer via a machine learning approach
who: L. Pappalardo, P. Cintia, P. Ferragina, E. Massucco, D. Pedreschi & F. Giannotti
venue: ACM Transactions on Intelligent Systems and Technology 10(5)
summary: Role-aware, multi-dimensional player rating learned from millions of Wyscout match events and compared with professional scouts' judgements.

title: A public data set of spatio-temporal match events in soccer competitions
who: L. Pappalardo, P. Cintia, A. Rossi, E. Massucco, P. Ferragina, D. Pedreschi & F. Giannotti
summary: Open Wyscout event logs for a full season of seven competitions: five top European leagues (2017/18), Euro 2016 and the 2018 World Cup.

title: Google Research Football: a novel reinforcement learning environment
who: K. Kurach, A. Raichuk, P. Stańczyk et al.
summary: Open-source physics-based 3D football simulator and RL benchmark, from single-skill scenarios to full 11-vs-11 games.

title: Deep soccer analytics: learning an action-value function for evaluating soccer players
who: G. Liu, Y. Luo, O. Schulte & T. Kharrat
summary: Learned a deep reinforcement-learning action-value (Q) function from play-by-play event sequences to evaluate players' actions.

title: Metrica Sports sample tracking and event data
who: Metrica Sports
summary: Openly released anonymised full-match tracking and event data, used in Friends of Tracking tutorials.

title: Friends of Tracking
who: Club analysts and academics (D. Sumpter, L. Shaw, J. Fernández, W. Spearman et al.)
summary: Free lecture videos and Python/R code on tracking and event data, recorded during the April-May 2020 COVID-19 lockdown.

title: LaurieOnTracking
who: Laurie Shaw
summary: Tutorial Python code for Metrica tracking data: velocities, Spearman-style pitch control and expected possession value.

title: kloppy
who: PySport (K. Vossen et al.)
summary: Python library that loads event and tracking data from many providers into standardised data models.

title: mplsoccer
who: A. Rowlinson & A. Durgapal
summary: Matplotlib-based Python library for drawing football pitches, pass maps, heatmaps and radar charts.

title: SkillCorner open data
who: SkillCorner
summary: Open broadcast-derived tracking data for 10 matches.

title: SoccerNet-v2: a dataset and benchmarks for holistic understanding of broadcast soccer videos
who: A. Deliège, A. Cioppa, S. Giancola et al.
summary: Extended SoccerNet's 500 games with denser annotations and benchmarks for action spotting, camera-shot segmentation and replay grounding.

title: Game Plan: what AI can do for football, and what football can do for AI
who: K. Tuyls, S. Omidshafiei, P. Muller et al.
summary: DeepMind position paper framing football as an AI testbed combining statistical learning, game theory and computer vision.

title: On-Ball Value (OBV)
who: StatsBomb (Hudl StatsBomb)
summary: Possession-value model scoring each on-ball event by its change in a team's likelihood of scoring and conceding, trained on StatsBomb xG.

title: worldfootballR
who: J. Zivkovic
summary: R package for extracting football data from FBref, Transfermarkt and Understat.

title: penaltyblog
who: M. Eastwood
summary: Python package for football match models (including Poisson and Dixon-Coles), team ratings, data scraping and betting-odds utilities.

title: floodlight: a high-level, data-driven sports analytics framework
who: D. Raabe, H. Biermann, M. Bassek et al.
summary: Python framework for loading, processing and analysing team-sport tracking and event data with unified data structures.

title: Seq2Event: learning the language of soccer using transformer-based match event prediction
who: I. Simpson, R. J. Beal, D. Locke & T. J. Norman
summary: Transformer-based sequence model predicting the next match event from preceding events, treating event streams like language.

title: From motor control to team play in simulated humanoid football
who: S. Liu, G. Lever, Z. Wang et al.
summary: Simulated humanoid players learned from joint-level control to coordinated team play through imitation and multi-agent reinforcement learning.

title: Semi-automated offside technology and connected ball at the 2022 World Cup
who: FIFA
summary: Twelve roof-mounted cameras tracking 29 body points per player plus an IMU in the Al Rihla ball (500 Hz) supported offside decisions.

title: un-xPass: measuring soccer player's creativity
who: P. Robberechts, M. Van Roy & J. Davis
summary: Measured creativity as passes that differ from the typical choice yet promise better outcomes, using StatsBomb 360 data and three ML models.

title: databallpy
who: A. Oonk
summary: Python package to load, preprocess, synchronise and visualise soccer event and tracking data.

title: TacticAI: an AI assistant for football tactics
who: Z. Wang, P. Veličković, D. Hennes et al.
summary: Geometric deep learning on corner kicks, built with Liverpool FC experts, predicting receivers and shots and generating alternative player setups.

title: SoccerNet Game State Reconstruction: end-to-end athlete tracking and identification on a minimap
who: V. Somers, V. Joos, A. Cioppa, S. Giancola et al.
summary: Benchmark and baseline for reconstructing players' pitch positions, roles, teams and jersey numbers on a minimap from broadcast video.

title: Towards a foundation large events model for soccer
who: T. Mendes-Neves, L. Meireles & J. Mendes-Moreira
summary: Porto/INESC TEC Large Events Model that simulates match event sequences from a game state; applied to xP+, players' contribution to points.

title: MatchTime: towards automatic soccer game commentary generation
who: J. Rao, H. Wu, C. Liu, Y. Wang & W. Xie
summary: Realigned SoccerNet commentary timestamps with video and trained a video-language model to generate match commentary.

title: How to Win the Premier League: The Inside Story of Football's Data Revolution
who: Ian Graham
summary: Account by Liverpool FC's director of research (2012-2023) of how the club used data in recruitment and decision-making.

title: An integrated dataset of spatiotemporal and event data in elite soccer
who: M. Bassek, R. Rein, H. Weber & D. Memmert
summary: Official event and position data from seven Bundesliga and 2. Bundesliga matches, released under CC-BY 4.0.
